questions.prompt: A price file arrives with 2025-03-04 above 2025-03-03. What does `sort_index` do with it?
options: It sorts the rows by close price, lowest first
It puts the rows in date order, so 2025-03-03 comes first
It removes the row that is out of place
It stops the program with an error
questions.explanation: The dates are the time index, so sorting the index puts the rows in date order. Nothing is removed; a later assert stops the program only for duplicates, missing values or impossible bars.

questions.prompt: A bar has open 102.0, close 104.0 and high 103.0. Which check in `load_bars` fails?
options: The check that the index is unique
The check that no value is missing
The check that the low is at most the open and the close
The check that the high is at least the open and the close
questions.explanation: The high is the highest trade of the period, so it cannot be below the close of 104.0. A high of 103.0 is impossible, so the high check stops the program.

questions.prompt: Why does `load_bars` stop the program on a duplicated date instead of carrying on?
options: Because a duplicated day is counted twice by the replay and changes the result without any message
Because pandas cannot store two rows with the same date
Because a duplicated date always means the close is missing
Because exchanges never trade twice on one day
questions.explanation: The replay believes every row. A day that appears twice counts twice, and nothing warns you, so the assert turns that silent error into a loud one at load time.
